'''Charles Pierre Chauvel''' (born 16 April 1969) is a New Zealand lawyer and former politician who was a Labour list [[Member of parliament|Member of Parliament]] (2006–2013) until his resignation to take up a position with the [[United Nations Development Programme|UN Development Programme]].<ref>[http://www.dia.govt.nz/MSOS118/On-Line/NZGazette.nsf/6cee7698a9bbc7cfcc256d510059ed0b/2037eb97485d5213cc257b2c005d732f!OpenDocument "Notice of Vacancy in Seat in House of Representatives"] (12 March 2013) 28 ''[[The New Zealand Gazette]]'' 889.</ref> He was the first New Zealand MP of Tahitian ancestry.

==Early years==
Born and raised in [[Gisborne, New Zealand|Gisborne]], he was awarded dux of [[Gisborne Boys' High School]]. While studying at the [[University of Auckland]], Chauvel captained the University's winning [[University Challenge (New Zealand)|University Challenge]] team in 1987.<ref name="TVNZ_800660">{{cite web |url=http://tvnz.co.nz/close-up/tue-aug-01-charles-chauvel-product-placement-800660/video |title=Close Up: Charles Chauvel; Product Placement |date=1 August 2006 |work=[[Television New Zealand]] |accessdate=23 September 2011}}</ref> He was involved in student politics having been appointed as National Affairs Officer for the [[Auckland University Students' Association]] in 1987. Chauvel graduated with a Bachelor of Laws (with Honours) from [[Victoria University of Wellington]] in 1989, and a Master of Jurisprudence (with Distinction) in 1994 from the University of Auckland.<ref>{{Cite thesis |title=Frustrated Fairness: Aspects of the Law relating to Compensation for Redundancy in New Zealand |url= https://books.google.com/books?id=CDKHtgAACAAJ |last=Chauvel |first=Charles |year=1994 |publisher=[[University of Auckland]]|oclc=153933067}}</ref>

In addition, the [[International Training Centre of the ILO]] in Turin (Italy) awarded Chauvel the Diploma in International Labour Standards in 2001,<ref>'The Achievers' Column', ''National Business Review'', 17 August 2001, p. 38</ref> and he also holds a Certificate in [[Health economics|Health Economics]] (with Merit) from Victoria University of Wellington (awarded 1993) along with a Certificate in [[Public International Law]] from the [[Hague Academy of International Law]] (1997).

==Legal career==
He was admitted as Barrister and Solicitor of the High Court of New Zealand in 1990, and to the [[New South Wales]] (Australia) Bar in 2003.

He wrote the re-issued Public Safety Title and served as consulting editor for a re-issue of the Gaming Law Title in the Laws of New Zealand Legal Encyclopedia. Chauvel has also co-authored two books, the ''New Zealand Employment Law Guide'' (LexisNexis, 2002) and ''Employment Mediation'' (Thomson Brookers, 2005).<ref>[http://www.minterellison.co.nz/newsdetail/pi_newsitemid/48 Minter Ellison Rudd Watts News] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110719062401/http://www.minterellison.co.nz/newsdetail/pi_newsitemid/48|date=19 July 2011}}; [https://books.google.com/books?id=IYJCAQAACAAJ]</ref> Prior to entering Parliament, Chavuel was on the board of Minter Ellison Rudd Watts (2003–2005) and became a partner in the Minter Ellison Legal Group in 2000. The 2005/06 edition of the ''Asia Pacific Legal 500'' listed him as a "Leading Individual" in employment law.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legal500.com/about |title=Legal500 |publisher=Legal500 |accessdate=19 February 2013}}</ref>

==Other involvements==
Chauvel was a board member of the New Zealand Aids Foundation from 1990 to 1994, serving as chair in 1996. He was appointed in 1995 to the Board of the New Zealand Public Health Commission; as Deputy Chair of the [[New Zealand Lotteries Commission]], and as Deputy Chair of [[Meridian Energy]] in 2005, having served as a director of that company from 2002.

[[File:Helen Clark and Charles Chauvel.jpg|thumb|With former New Zealand Prime Minister [[Helen Clark]]]]

A member of the Labour Party since 1985, Chauvel has held a number of Labour Party positions including Chair of the [[Princes Street Branch]], President of [[Young Labour (New Zealand)|Young Labour]] (then known as Labour Socialist Youth), membership of the Party's controlling body (the New Zealand Council) and Policy council and co-Chair of [[Rainbow Labour]].

Chauvel stood as Labour's electoral candidate for {{NZ electorate link|Maramarua}}, in [[1990 New Zealand general election|1990]] losing to the [[New Zealand National Party|National Party]]'s [[Bill Birch]]. He next stood in [[2005 New Zealand general election|2005]] as Labour's candidate for [[Ohariu-Belmont]], then losing to [[United Future]] leader [[Peter Dunne]].<ref>{{cite web |date=21 March 2005 |title=Talented Kiwis dominate Labour list |url=http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA0503/S00439.htm |accessdate=20 December 2009 |publisher=Scoop NZ}}</ref> However, he was able to become a list MP on 1 August 2006 when [[Jim Sutton]] retired.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA0607/S00121.htm |title=Hon Jim Sutton retires |publisher=Scoop NZ|date=10 July 2006|accessdate=20 December 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url= http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO0607/S00372.htm |title=New List MP For Labour Party|publisher=Scoop NZ|date=31 August 2006|accessdate=20 December 2009}}</ref> He sought the Labour candidacy in [[Wellington Central (New Zealand electorate)|Wellington Central]] ahead of the 2008 election but withdrew.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2009-01-31 |title=Chauvel stands aside in Wellington Central |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/38181/Chauvel-stands-aside-in-Wellington-Central |access-date=2022-08-29 |website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |language=en}}</ref> Chauvel lost twice more to Dunne in the reconfigured [[Ōhāriu (New Zealand electorate)|Ōhariu]] electorate in [[2008 New Zealand general election|2008]] and [[2011 New Zealand general election|2011]], but was elected on both occasions as a list MP.

In his first term of Parliament—the last of the [[Fifth Labour Government of New Zealand|Fifth Labour Government]]—Chauvel was a member of the Commerce Committee and the Government Administration committee from August 2006 to February 2007, and thereafter chair of the [[Finance and Expenditure Committee|Finance and Expenditure committee]] and a member of the Justice committee until October 2008.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Chauvel, Charles - New Zealand Parliament |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/mps-and-electorates/former-members-of-parliament/chauvel-charles/ |access-date=2022-08-29 |website=www.parliament.nz |language=en}}</ref> He was also parliamentary private secretary to the Attorney-General in 2008, although his appointment to the role was delayed from the Government's late-2007 reshuffle because Chauvel announced he would be accepting the position before it had been officially confirmed.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Labour list MP jumps the gun - New Zealand News |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/labour-list-mp-jumps-the-gun/TN4DBNV5JJMU5OMTAJ23DZ2XJI/ |access-date=2022-08-29 |website=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |language=en-NZ}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2009-01-31 |title=Ambitious Chauvel angers PM in reshuffle |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/733/Ambitious-Chauvel-angers-PM-in-reshuffle |access-date=2022-08-29 |website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |language=en}}</ref>

In Labour's opposition years, he held party spokesperson roles for energy, climate change and the environment from 2008 until 2011,<ref name="NZ_Herald_10544077">{{cite news |date=20 November 2008 |title=Five newcomers in Labour's shadow Cabinet |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz-election-2008/news/article.cfm?c_id=1501799&objectid=10544077 |accessdate=23 September 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=10 June 2010 |title=Fresh look for Labour's shadow Cabinet |publisher=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/3811449/Fresh-look-for-Labours-shadow-Cabinet |accessdate=15 June 2010}}</ref> and for justice and the arts from 2011 until 2013.<ref>{{cite news |date=3 February 2011 |title=Labour Caucus – 2011 |publisher=scoop.co.nz |url=http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA1102/S00048/labour-caucus-2011.htm |accessdate=15 February 2011}}</ref> He was shadow attorney-general and chair of the privileges committee from 2011 to 2013.<ref name=":0" /> He supported [[David Cunliffe]] over [[David Shearer]] in the [[2011 New Zealand Labour Party leadership election|Labour Party leadership election of 2011]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-02-20 |title=MP quits ahead of reshuffle |url=https://www.odt.co.nz/news/politics/mp-quits-ahead-reshuffle |access-date=2022-08-29 |website=[[Otago Daily Times]] |language=en}}</ref>

On 19 February 2013, Chauvel announced his resignation from parliament, effective 11 March, to take a job working at the [[United Nations Development Programme]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Labour MP Chauvel resigns for UN |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/labour-mp-charles-chauvel-resigns/O5LDLFMUHH4J4S7HPORARILCKQ/ |access-date=2022-08-29 |website=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=19 February 2013 |language=en-NZ}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{cite news |last=Trevett |first=Claire |date=19 February 2013 |title=Labour MP Charles Chauvel resigns |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=10866354 |accessdate=22 May 2020}}</ref> He gave his valedictory statement on 27 February 2013.<ref>{{cite hansard|title=Valedictory Statements|jurisdiction=New Zealand|house=House of Representatives|date=23 February 2013|volume=687|url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/document/50HansS_20130227_00001068/chauvel-charles-valedictory-statements|speaker=Charles Chauvel|position=list MP|page=8284}}</ref> He was succeeded in parliament by the next candidate on the Labour [[party list]], [[Carol Beaumont]].<ref>{{cite news |date=13 March 2013 |title=Carol Beaumont takes a new seat in Parlliament |publisher=[[Radio New Zealand]] |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/130264/carol-beaumont-takes-a-new-seat-in-parlliament |accessdate=22 May 2020}}</ref>

===Repeal of the Provocation Defence===
{{Main|Gay panic defense#New Zealand|l1 = Gay Panic Defence}}

Provocation, as a defence to murder, was publicised in New Zealand due to the high-profile trials of [[Murder of Sophie Elliott|Clayton Weatherston]] in 2008 and Ferdinand Ambach in 2009, both of whom attempted to plead provocation in court (the latter successfully). The Law Commission, in its 2007 [https://web.archive.org/web/20100524004417/http://www.lawcom.govt.nz/ProjectReport.aspx?ProjectID=138 report on the issue], had argued for repeal of the defence. Chauvel drafted a [[Private member's bill|member's bill]] to repeal the provocation defence in 2009,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2009-07-10 |title=Labour MP seeks to remove provocation as defence |url=https://www.odt.co.nz/news/politics/labour-mp-seeks-remove-provocation-defence |access-date=2022-08-29 |website=[[Otago Daily Times]] |language=en}}</ref> although a separate Government bill was later introduced and passed in November 2009 by 116 votes to five; the [[ACT Party]] voicing the only opposition.<ref name="provo2">{{cite news |date=27 November 2009 |title=Provocation defence repeal 'knee-jerk reaction' |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/politics/news/article.cfm?c_id=280&objectid=10612028&pnum=1 |accessdate=23 September 2011}}</ref>

== International roles ==
In February 2009, he and the former leader of the New Zealand Labour Party, [[Helen Clark]], were appointed as New Zealand's inaugural representatives on the Board of the Pacific Friends of the Global Fund, the regional partnership with the [[Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation]]'s major initiative against HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gaynz.com/articles/publish/2/article_7368.php|title=Chauvel to promote Global Fund in Pacific|publisher=GayNZ.com|date=27 April 2009|accessdate=20 December 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090430141622/http://www.gaynz.com/articles/publish/2/article_7368.php|archive-date=30 April 2009|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In June 2010, Chauvel was appointed as a member of the United Nations Global Commission on HIV and the Law.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://home.nzcity.co.nz/news/article.aspx?id=116430&fm=newsmain,nrhl |title=Chauvel on global HIV commission |publisher=nzcity.co.nz |date=25 June 2010|accessdate=29 June 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.3news.co.nz/Labour-MP-Chauvel-appointed-to-new-UN-commission/tabid/419/articleID/162663/Default.aspx?ArticleID=162663 |title=Labour MP Chauvel appointed to new UN commission |publisher=3news.co.nz |date=25 June 2010 |accessdate=29 June 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120908071327/http://www.3news.co.nz/Labour-MP-Chauvel-appointed-to-new-UN-commission/tabid/419/articleID/162663/Default.aspx?ArticleID=162663 |archive-date=8 September 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

After leaving Parliament, Chauvel worked for the [[United Nations Development Programme]] in New York<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> and then as the United Nations Asia and Pacific regional ombudsman.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thepost.co.nz/nz-news/350156526/life-after-politics-finding-new-buzz-beyond-beehive |title=Life after politics: Finding a new buzz beyond the Beehive |first=Julie |last=Julie Jacobson |work=[[The Post (New Zealand newspaper)|The Post]] |date=27 January 2024 |accessdate=27 January 2024}}</ref>
